children: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.
Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block.

The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent.
The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.
Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on September 22, 2025.

title: ONGC takes charge of Cambay block as Vedanta records ₹379 crore impairment
